occupation: Experimental Physicist, Nuclear Physicist, Particle Physicist
school: Nuclear Physics, Particle Physics, Experimental Physics
legacy: Chien-Shiung Wu is widely regarded as one of the greatest experimental physicists of the twentieth century. Her definitive experimental proof that parity is not conserved in weak nuclear interactions transformed particle physics and overturned a long-held assumption about the symmetries of nature. Her achievements established new foundations for modern physics and earned her recognition as the 'First Lady of Physics' and the 'Queen of Nuclear Research'.
earlyLife: Wu was born in Liuhe, Taicang, Jiangsu Province, China. Her father strongly supported education and founded a school that encouraged girls to pursue academic excellence. She studied physics at National Central University before moving to the United States to continue her education at the University of California, Berkeley, where she earned her doctorate under Ernest Lawrence. Her exceptional experimental skills became evident early in her scientific career.
scientificField: Physics, Nuclear Physics, Particle Physics, Experimental Physics
majorContributions: Wu made important contributions to nuclear physics, beta decay, radioactive isotopes, and the Manhattan Project during World War II. Her most famous achievement was the 1956 Wu Experiment, which demonstrated that parity symmetry is violated in weak nuclear interactions. This result confirmed the theoretical prediction of Tsung-Dao Lee and Chen-Ning Yang and fundamentally changed the understanding of subatomic physics. Her experiments became models of precision and rigor, setting new standards for experimental research in physics.
laterLife: Wu spent most of her career at Columbia University, where she became one of the world's leading physicists and an influential educator. She served as the first woman president of the American Physical Society and received numerous honors including the National Medal of Science and the inaugural Wolf Prize in Physics. Throughout her life she advocated for scientific excellence and greater opportunities for women in science.
whyImportant: Chien-Shiung Wu's experimental discoveries reshaped modern particle physics. By proving parity violation, she helped reveal that nature behaves differently than physicists had previously believed. Her work contributed to the development of the Standard Model of particle physics and deepened scientific understanding of fundamental forces. Beyond her scientific achievements, she became an enduring symbol of excellence, perseverance, and equality in science.
